newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Settlers mourn Hebron's handover to "terrorists".
newsitem.headline: Settlers mourn Hebron's handover to "terrorists".

text.p: Some 2,000 settlers gathered in Hebron on Monday to mourn Israel's handover of most of the West Bank town to Palestinian forces the settlers called "terrorist organisations and murderers".
The sombre gathering after sundown in a cold drizzle stood in stark contrast to Palestinian celebrations over the weekend to mark their liberation from 30 years of Israeli occupation.
The settlers huddled under umbrellas outside the Tomb of the Patriarchs where the biblical Abraham and his family are buried, reciting psalms of mourning over the city's division.
Israel retains control of one fifth of the city, including the homes of 400 Jews and 20,000 Palestinians. It also controls the tomb, holy to both Jews and Moslems.

"We are here to express our pain the city was handed to the control of terrorist organisations and murderers," said Noam Arnon, a spokesman for Hebron settlers, addressing the crowd. "How much this hurts."

"The (biblical) mothers and fathers are the mothers and fathers of all the people of Israel for generations past, for generations to come and for this generation. We will stay here, we will build here, we will strengthen here," Arnon said.

While the settlers mourned, Palestinians set off two firecrackers from a nearby hill, a remnant from the festivities that culminated in a victory address by Palestinian President Yasser Arafat on Sunday.

Hebron has been a frequent flashpoint of Israeli-Arab violence. The handover last Friday was the fruit of months of acrimonious negotiations over maintaining Israeli control of the Jewish enclave inside the Palestinian city of 100,000.

After their celebrations died down, Palestinians were frustrated to discover the city was now dotted with Israeli checkpoints on all roads between the Israeli and PLO-controlled areas, clogging roads in a town unaccustomed to traffic laws.
"How can we live like this? How can we live if the situation stays like this?" asked taxi driver Hamdi Marrar.
A line of more than 50 Palestinian cars clogged one narrow road snaking up a hill from one checkpoint set up a stone's throw from the Jewish settler enclave in the city's heart.
"I drove my taxi 20 or 30 times between this side and the Israeli side today. They stopped me every time even though they recognise me," Marrar, 33, said.
"Where is the redeployment? This is like a new prison."

But unlike the 30 years Hebron was under Israeli occupation, Marrar had an ear ready to hear his complaint. The taxi driver aired his grievance to a nearby Palestinian policeman, who quickly conveyed the gripe to an Israeli soldier fanning cars through a plastic barricade.
Four hundred Palestinian police entered the city on Friday to the cheers of Arab residents.
New Israeli barricades were not the only problem confronting Hebronite motorists on Monday. Palestinians butted heads with PLO police deployed to direct cars in Hebron's often chaotic streets.
One angry policeman left his intersection to chase down a motorist who whizzed by his post after ignoring orders to stop.
"All day long," the officer muttered.

Palestinian and Israeli troops launched two new joint patrols in the PLO-held part of Hebron on Monday. Orange flagged Israeli jeeps trailed a Palestinian escort along a hilltop road overlooking a Jewish settler enclave.
The joint patrols do not tour Israeli-occupied areas.
"Everything is fine. The patrols are very professional and we are in cooperation with the Israelis," Khaled Da'ajneh, wearing a crisp Palestinian uniform, told Reuters.
